text:
Recent work supports separating directional transitions from general similarity. [TransGAT (ICDM 2024)](https://www.amazon.science/publications/transitivity-encoded-graph-attention-networks-for-complementary-item-recommendations) encodes behavioral direction, jointly learns complement/substitute graphs, and uses self-supervised augmentation. Its substitute supervision cannot simply be assumed available here. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.09209v1) offers a cheaper starting point: project training interactions into a weighted item graph, then adjust edges using chronological order and bounded time windows. This captures asymmetry without pretrained encoders, though observed purchase order remains a proxy for complementarity.

[MMSC (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22268v1) combines metadata with self-supervised behavior denoising and relation-specific representations, emphasizing noisy associations and sparse items. Its full method uses a multimodal foundation model and LLM-generated augmentation, making it unsuitable under the stated restrictions. Transferable ideas are separate relation heads, confidence-weighted behavioral supervision, and content/interaction fusion; its reported gains do not establish performance for a scratch-trained text replacement.

Practical research hypothesis: retain SASRec and add a small asymmetric transition scorer using separate source/target projections, plus TF-IDF or hashed title/description n-grams projected into trainable embeddings. Train auxiliary forward-transition prediction and masked-text reconstruction using training data only; treat lexical similarity as a soft similarity signal, never a substitute label. Missing descriptions/specifications should reduce confidence or trigger an interaction-only fallback. These are proposed adaptations, not verified findings: neither temporal adjacency nor shared words establishes functional complementarity or hardware compatibility. Compare transition-only, text-only, and combined variants using the fixed macro validation HR@10.
